intro.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, accessible form component that collects user information. You will learn the core concepts of web accessibility (a11y), focusing on semantic HTML, proper labeling, and keyboard navigation. The main technologies involved are Vue's template syntax, native HTML form elements, and ARIA attributes. By the end, you'll understand how to make your Vue applications usable for everyone, including people with disabilities.
intro.usecase: Accessibility fundamentals are essential in any public-facing web application to ensure all users, including those with disabilities, can interact with your product. For example, in a SaaS dashboard, proper ARIA labels on charts, keyboard navigation through data tables, and semantic HTML for filter panels allow screen reader users to understand and control the interface. As a developer, implementing these a11y patterns in Vue components—like accessible form validation messages or focus-trapped modals—is a standard requirement for compliance and inclusive user experience in real projects such as e-commerce sites, banking apps, or content management systems.
